# Diana Tofan

> Design engineer and product designer based in Copenhagen, Denmark. I design and prototype in code, mostly for complex systems: internal tools, observability, LiveOps and platform workflows. Currently a Product Designer at Tactile Games (2024 to present). Previously a UX Engineer at Google (2022 to 2024) and a UX/UI Designer at Famly.

Some case studies are partly password protected on the site. Each summary below is public and matches the numbers on the page.

## Case studies

- [Diana's Diamonds, a prototype library for AI-driven design](https://dianatofan.net/work/dianas-diamonds): Tactile Games, September to October 2026. Product Designer and Design Engineer. Designers at Tactile build prototypes by asking Claude Code to change the real codebase, so prototypes piled up in separate repos and got deleted. I built one library and hub for all of them: a 3D field and a searchable grid, a walkthrough of what each prototype changes, links to tickets, and a diff developers can build from. Six Claude Code skills cover setup to handoff; Claude can open pull requests but never merge. Alvaro Hernandez helped set up the infrastructure. Results: 16 prototypes in one library in five weeks, 9 done or merged, and a library that kept running after I left.
- [LiveOps at Tactile: game setup automation and alerting](https://dianatofan.net/work/liveops-tooling): Tactile Games, 2025. Two separate projects on the internal LiveOps Dashboard, presented on one page. Product Designer on both. (1) Game setup automation, 3 months, with a PM, a tech lead and 3 engineers: every new game had to be registered by hand across LiveOps, analytics, build pipelines, permissions and infrastructure, so I designed a guided four-step setup flow with automated provisioning and clear post-launch ownership. Shipped. Results: about 2x faster game setup and 3 more games launched per quarter. (2) LiveOps alerting, 3 months, with a PM, the CTO and 3 engineers: creators had no view of backend failures inside the Dashboard, so I redesigned it to surface them early with a critical issues banner, persistent sidebar signals, issue lists with ownership and watchers, and notification settings. Shipped. Results: critical failures detected in minutes instead of hours, 22% fewer production incidents, less reliance on Slack and external monitoring.
- [Travel planning on Google Search](https://dianatofan.net/work/travel-planning): Google, summer 2024. UX Engineer with 3 UX designers, a UX researcher and a PM. Search handled single queries, not the multi-session reality of planning a trip. We defined a planning framework (get inspired, look into alternatives, rediscover the journey) and I built React prototypes with real Maps data for user testing. Concept work. Results: validated by UX leadership and fed into the 2024 Google Search roadmap shift toward more visual results.
- [Famly design system](https://dianatofan.net/work/design-system): Famly, 2024. UX/UI Designer, 3 months. An off-the-shelf UI kit had turned into inconsistent patterns and rising support calls. I built and rolled out a design system the team owns. Shipped. Results: 35% faster UI development and 18% fewer support calls.
- [Release timeline](https://dianatofan.net/work/release-timeline): Tactile Games, 2026. A release timeline inside the LiveOps Dashboard, prototyped in code, to show release impact across live games and cut debugging time.

## Side projects

- [Money Jenga](https://dianatofan.net/work/money-jenga): an iPhone budget app where every purchase pulls a block out of a tower of cash. SwiftUI, SpriteKit, SwiftData with CloudKit, built with Claude Code.
- [Golden Goose Digital Museum](https://dianatofan.net/work/golden-goose-museum): seven low-poly 3D Superstar sneakers and a browser-based part painter with an AI magic wand and Apple Pencil support.
- [Beouf Salad Decorator](https://dianatofan.net/work/boeuf-salad-decorator): a web app that turns the Romanian tradition of over-decorated Christmas salads into shareable retro holiday cards.
- [Human Redundancy Terminal](https://dianatofan.github.io/risk-assessment-terminal): a glitchy CRT terminal built with Kaggle data and Google AI Studio.
